answer: One sybil defense is a throughput-capped activation queue. New identities dock at a wharf and wait in FIFO; a small fixed quota activates per epoch. Queue-jumping costs a rising entry toll that is fully burned, echoing an auction. Each pending identity pays an upkeep burn per epoch, so dormant clones bleed cost for months before gaining vote weight. Honest newcomers pay nothing and simply wait. With entries settled in umber ink, influence cannot be minted faster than the queue admits - costs grow linearly with every fake agent, payoffs only after activation. Mass cloning stays unprofitable.
